correctness.rationale: A site-labelled Voronoi cell is the intersection of two origin-centered bisector hemispheres and hence a spherical lune of perimeter 2π and area 2(π-Θ). For fixed tagged north-pole site the independent bisector normals have density (e·n)_+/π; integrating their angle by the Gaussian ReLU positive-wedge formula gives an exact density and CDF [a(2+cos a)-3 sin a]/(6π), 0<a<2π. Independent SymPy integration confirms CDF derivative, E A=4π/3, second moment 20π²/9−10/3, P(A<=π)=1/6, variance 4π²/9−10/3; exchangeability and A1+A2+A3=4π give covariance 5/3−2π²/9. Proof is exact; simulations are not used as an unrestricted certificate.
residual_risks: Not a law for area-biased cell selection, 4+ sites, nonuniform samples, or full joint 3-area distribution.

originality.rationale: Kabluchko–Thäle give spherical binomial-Voronoi typical-cell face statistics in the same random-site model, and Cho–Saul already give the Gaussian angular kernel. Those inputs do not, in the inspected primary sections, give the complete area CDF/variance for a site-labelled 3-site cell; Li et al. concern random query-to-fixed-site nearest distances. A prior unindexed spherical-lune-area law remains possible.

The closed distribution, moments and covariance are natural exact benchmarks for random spherical tessellation.
residual_risks: Exact known premises and natural scope limitations are credited; no claim of broad priority or universal generalization.
